---
title: "Components"
subtitle: "The four shortcodes, and the attributes that shape them."
description: "Worked examples of the divider, value-box, progress, and badge shortcodes, with the defaults the code applies and the colour and icon values it accepts."
---

A component is written once and rendered by the format you produce.
The same source gives a Typst panel in a report and a styled `div` on a page.

The [Reference](../reference.qmd#shortcodes) lists every attribute and its default.
This page shows how each one is used, and what the code does with the value.

## Divider

A divider draws a horizontal rule across part of the page.

```markdown
{{{< divider >}}}

{{{< divider style="dashed" width="80%" >}}}

{{{< divider style="gradient" label="Results" >}}}

{{{< divider style="ornamental" thickness="3pt" >}}}
```

The `style` attribute takes `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `ornamental`, or `gradient`.

`thickness` and `width` become CSS custom properties in HTML output, `--divider-thickness` and `--divider-width`.
A thickness is any CSS length, and it defaults to `1pt`.
A width is a length or a percentage, and it defaults to `50%`.

The `label` attribute changes the markup, not only the text.
A divider with no label is an `<hr>` element.
A divider with a label is a `<div>` with `role="separator"`, and the label becomes the accessible name.

## Value box

A value box shows one number, with an optional unit, label, and icon.

```markdown
{{{< value-box value="99" unit="%" label="Coverage" colour="success" >}}}

{{{< value-box value="1240" label="Downloads" icon="up" colour="info" >}}}

{{{< value-box value="3" unit="ms" label="Latency" icon="down" colour="#74aadb" >}}}
```

### Icons

The `icon` attribute takes any single character, so an emoji works.
Three names are shortcuts:

- `up` gives an upward arrow.
- `down` gives a downward arrow.
- `stable` gives a horizontal bar.

A name that is not one of the three is used as the character itself.

### Colours

`colour` accepts one of ten theme names: `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `caution`, `neutral`, `subtle`, `emphasis`, `accent`, and `outline`.
It also accepts a colour value such as `#74aadb`.
`color` is accepted as a spelling of the same attribute.

## Progress

A progress bar shows a percentage.

```markdown
{{{< progress value="72" label="Progress" colour="info" >}}}

{{{< progress value="40" show-value="false" >}}}

{{{< progress value="95" height="0.6em" colour="success" >}}}
```

The `value` is clamped to the range 0 to 100, so a value outside it produces a full or an empty bar rather than an error.

`show-value` writes the percentage inside the bar, and is on unless the attribute is exactly `false`.

`height` is a CSS length.
Its default depends on the format: `1.5em` in HTML output, and `1.2em` in a Reveal.js deck.

A colour that is not a theme name and is a real colour value, such as a hex code, is passed through as the `--custom-colour` property instead of a theme class.

## Badge

A badge is an inline label.
It is the one component with two spellings, and the spelling depends on the output format.

```markdown
The build is {{{< badge text="passing" colour="success" >}}} today.
```

The shortcode produces nothing at all in Typst output.
Write the span form instead, which works in every format:

```markdown
The build is [passing]{.badge colour="success"} today.
```

The span takes `colour` and `icon`, and the badge text is the content of the span.
The shortcode takes the same two, and `text` carries the label.

::: {.callout-tip}

Use the span form everywhere if a document is rendered to more than one format.
It is the only form that survives all three.

:::

## Where the components appear

The [rendered report](../preview.pdf) on this site is built by `mcanouil-typst` as the site publishes, and it carries a value box, a progress bar, a divider, and a panel.
